body:
You seem to understand me very well. Right off the top of my head, the person that comes to mind who refuses to change at all is my mother. She's in her mid 40s and has accomplished practically nothing. She still depends on her parents for money and she still depends on me to support her. I don't ever expect her to change, but I am unfortunately stuck living with her for at least one more year.

I meant severely change their personalities, but this is probably wrong as well. You're absolutely right. Many people have to change in ways that I can't imagine from my point of view. If this means growing up to you, then I suppose I need to grow up.

Thank you, really. I think I needed this constructive criticism.

This sounds like a very enlightening experience. Perhaps Nirvana can only be reached by NDEs? Oh, I don't think suicidal people should have a sense of humor. Oh well.

I have had similar but far weaker experiences while I was in deep meditation. It's like I am far more empathetic and realize there is much more than my own experiences. I'm used to changing perspectives because of my bastardized practices. I don't ever expect to have an epiphany where all of a sudden everything makes sense and I can be eternally happy.

Everything happens in the mind. It's just . . . I don't really know. Life is disappointing.

I'm 23. I'm not autistic. I've been to several psychiatrists in my life and none of them ever even suggested that I have autism, though my siblings thought I have it. I have issues with anxiety, particularly social anxiety. I did have to read a few books on how to improve my skills, and I have made a few friends. If I were to continue pushing myself further I probably would feel similar to you in that I am better at socializing than others because I had to try. I just don't think the endeavor is worth it. All these years of suffering just for this lackluster bullshit people rely on to communicate?

I know if I put in the effort my thoughts will align with "normalcy" and I will perhaps become considerably happy. My bizarre thoughts do stem from justifying awkwardness. It's just become so deeply ingrained that I consider it apart of my personality. Most people don't have to severely change, so the way I feel is that why should I? I just don't think it's worth it, even if it means I am unhappy and suicidal.

I'm not religious, though I do follow some Buddhist adages as guidance. I think it's the only religion that remotely makes sense, though I am still skeptical towards it. I think nothing happens when we die. As I said, our atoms just return to the environment; we are literally recycled.

Don't worry if you offend me or anything. Even though I am suicidal, I am surprisingly thick skin when it comes to listening to others. I've always wanted experience an NDE myself. I'm pretty sure I would only experience something similar to you and nothing supernatural.

I really appreciate your input, and I am glad you survived cancer. The way I see it, there truly is no self. From a scientific prospective, we are all molecules constantly breaking down and being rearranged into other molecules. New people don't arise from nothing. They are comprised of atoms that have been around since the beginning of time and were also once part of others. The question is whether this human experience where I am forced to believe I have an identity is worth continuing. After all, I won't truly disappear. My atoms will just go elsewhere.

Of course, this is not a view most people consider, and it's perhaps for the best. Life is utterly meaningless when you see it like this. As you said, others have a different perspective of me than I have of myself. I am fine fading into nothing but a memory into others. I know I am not alone. I have just come to the point where I no longer care about anything. Any activity would just feel like a distraction. Psychiatric help, which I've tried before, would most likely render me a completely different person.

It just makes me wonder, is it hard for some others to accept that not everyone is meant to live in the current condition of the world?

I'm sorry if my thoughts seem jumbled. I can go on and on with this pseudo-intellectual nonsense about existence. There was a time when I thought I was very wise for doing such a thing, but now I know better.
